title: EFC — Hypothesis: Interrelation Between Energy and Entropy
description: Proposes Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), a framework in which universal expansion, structure formation, and phenomena attributed to dark matter/energy emerge from a universal energy Grid composed of Higgs-boson nodes, with energy flow declining linearly as entropy increases. The model treats the speed of light as an emergent property regulated by energy-flow gradients and makes falsifiable predictions in redshift profiles, gravitational lensing, and CMB anisotropies that can distinguish it from ΛCDM.

energy_entropy_linear_decline.description: Energy flow declines linearly with entropy from a singular state (S=0) to a maximum entropy state (S=1), posited to drive spacetime expansion.

emergent_speed_of_light.description: The effective speed of light is treated as an emergent property regulated by local energy-flow magnitude and gradients rather than a fundamental constant in all regimes.

grid_collapse_black_hole_condition.description: When energy-flow concentration surpasses a critical threshold, the Grid nodes collapse, destabilizing spacetime locally and forming black holes.

hubble_dependence_on_energy_flow.description: The Hubble expansion rate is proposed to be a function of the global energy-flow state rather than a constant term (Λ).

key_results.main_finding: Introduces a unified hypothesis in which entropy-driven energy flow across a Higgs-node Grid explains cosmic expansion, dark matter phenomenology, and an emergent speed of light, and outlines empirical tests via redshift, lensing, and CMB signatures.

sealed_predictions.statement: Redshift–distance relations in cosmic voids show nonlinear deviations from ΛCDM that correlate with regions of low energy flow (low E_f).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Cross-comparing SDSS void catalogs with galaxy and supernova redshift–distance measurements; testing for residuals after ΛCDM fits.

sealed_predictions.statement: Weak and strong gravitational lensing strengths exhibit environment-dependent anomalies tied to energy-flow gradients, beyond what baryons + ΛCDM predict.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Measuring lensing convergence and shear in SDSS/JWST fields, testing for residual correlations with environmental indicators (e.g., voids/halos) after ΛCDM modeling.

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB temperature anisotropies contain scale-dependent deviations consistent with entropy-driven structure formation from the Grid, distinct from ΛCDM fits.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Fitting Planck CMB spectra including EFC-motivated terms and testing whether they are required by the data or constrained to zero.

sealed_predictions.statement: Higgs-field stability metrics correlate with large-scale energy-flow anomalies if dark matter arises from non-resonant energy states in the Grid.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint analyses combining LHC Higgs property measurements with large-scale structure maps (SDSS/JWST) to search for predicted correlations.

kill_criteria: KC1: Precision redshift–distance measurements in low-density voids (SDSS and follow-ups) show no statistically significant nonlinear deviations from ΛCDM after accounting for known systematics, eliminating the proposed E_f correlation.

KC2: Gravitational lensing convergence and shear maps (SDSS/JWST) are fully explained by baryonic matter + standard cold dark matter with no residual dependence on environmental proxies of energy flow or entropy gradients.

KC3: Planck CMB temperature and lensing power spectra are consistent with ΛCDM across all relevant multipoles, with any EFC-motivated parameters constrained to null values and providing no improvement in fit quality.

KC4: Direct detection of dark matter as a particle with electromagnetic interactions or scattering properties incompatible with the non-resonant Higgs-node energy-state interpretation (e.g., confirmed EM-coupling inconsistent with EFC).

KC5: High-precision measurements of Higgs properties (mass, self-coupling, potential shape) from LHC/HL-LHC exclude the stability and non-resonant behavior required for Higgs bosons to serve as discrete Grid nodes at cosmological scales.

KC6: Time-of-flight constraints from multi-messenger events (e.g., LIGO–EM counterparts) and astrophysical propagation tests find no environment-dependent propagation effects where EFC requires an emergent, gradient-regulated effective c.
